chunks: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him):

'(He) desires, and intends, and determines, and ordains?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And He loves?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'And how does He desire, and intend, and determine, and ordain, while not loving?' He said: 'This is how it has come to us.'

key_terms.أَحَبَّ: Divine love (mahabba): God's normative approval and love, distinct from His will
key_terms.أَرَادَ: Divine intention (irada): God's specific intention or will, often distinguished from mashi'a in theological discourse
key_terms.شَاءَ: Divine will/desire (mashi'a): God's primordial volition encompassing all that exists
key_terms.قَدَّرَ: Divine determination (qadar): God's measure and assignment of all things in creation
key_terms.قَضَى: Divine decree (qada'): God's final decree and ordainment of events

ai.seo_question: Does Allah love everything He wills and decrees according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether God's will and decree necessarily entail His love for what He has ordained. The Imam confirms that God desires, intends, determines, and ordains all things, yet does not necessarily love everything He has decreed — a profound distinction between God's ontological will that encompasses all of existence and His normative approval that is reserved for obedience and righteousness. The Imam's closing remark 'This is how it has come to us' indicates this is received doctrinal teaching transmitted through the Imams.
